content.en: Scheduled Commercial Banks (SCBs) are the primary financial intermediaries in India. To be classified as 'scheduled', a bank must satisfy the conditions laid down in the **Second Schedule of the RBI Act, 1934**. These banks are required to maintain a certain level of **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)** and **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** as mandated by the RBI.
